claims.text: CFOP is a common method: Cross, First Two Layers, Orient Last Layer, Permute Last Layer. The cross solves four edges around a center with matching side colors, not a whole face. A PLL skip needs no permutation algorithm after orientation because pieces already have the correct relative positions; an upper-face alignment may remain. A scramble sequence sets up the starting state. A double extended cross additionally solves two corner-edge pairs.

claims.text: The registered method centers successful log times within solver-rounds, controls global attempt position and corrects finite-peer noise. It excludes the focal solver’s entire final before estimating the shared scheduled-position contrast; selects the observed fastest successful eligible final solve per solver-season; does not select the fastest adjusted solve; and aggregates adjusted/observed ratios geometrically with equal solver-season weight. R and F answer different questions. The original gate failed; an owner-approved pre-confirmation amendment validated recentered R uncertainty under specified simulations. The fixed-selection interval is sensitivity only. F and R are success-only; the DNF endpoint is separate. Slot conditions, replacement mapping and residual variation prevent attributing total personal luck or a particular record.
